programs.name: Strength Formula
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A 4-day upper/lower strength block built around the big barbell lifts. Two pressing days (bench-led, then overhead-press-led) and two pulling/lower days (squat-led, then deadlift-led). Every session opens with a heavy main lift in the 2-5 rep range and is backed off with strength-hypertrophy accessories. Run it for 4 weeks, adding a little load each week while keeping the top sets sharp and leaving a rep in reserve.

programs.name: Wild Odds Split
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A 5-day body-part split pairing heavy, low-rep compound work with high-volume hypertrophy accessories: a squat-led quad day, a shoulders and core day, a back and triceps day, a hamstrings/glutes/groin day built around deadlifts, and a chest and biceps finisher. Run it for 4 weeks, adding load on the main lifts (Back Squat, Overhead Press, Deadlift) each week.

programs.name: Wave Strength 5s-3s-1s
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A classic percentage-wave strength template: one main lift per day, three waved work sets, and an all-out AMRAP top set to drive progress. Cycles a 5s week → 3s week → 5s/3s/1s week → deload. All loads are prescribed as percentages and prefill from YOUR 1RMs (set them in Profile) — the waves run off a Training Max of 90% of your true 1RM, and the numbers here are already converted. After each cycle, add 2.5 kg to upper-body and 5 kg to lower-body maxes and run it again.

programs.name: 6-Week Bench-Focus Hybrid
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A 6-week linear block in a bench-focused hybrid layout - extra bench frequency on top of the upper/lower structure. The block waves from muscular conditioning (wk1-2) through a linear max-OT phase (wk3), heavy acclimation (wk4), high-intensity strength (wk5) and a peak/test week (wk6). Main lifts are prescribed as a %1RM each week, so set your Squat / Bench / Deadlift 1RMs in Profile and the app fills your working weights. Per-set schemes and the MR / back-off protocols are in each exercise's notes. Loads are percent-based and prefill from your bench (and squat/deadlift) 1RMs — set them in Profile.

programs.name: Russian Squat Routine
programs.author: Classic Soviet template
programs.description: The classic 6-week, 18-session Soviet peaking cycle: three weeks of brutal volume at 80%, then an intensity ladder — 85% 5×5, 90% 4×4, 95% 3×3, 100% 2×2 — ending in a new max attempt at 105%. Built for the squat, but when you start it you can run the whole cycle on another lift instead (bench, overhead press, or deadlift — deadlift only if you recover like a mutant). Loads prefill from your 1RM in Profile.

programs.name: Aaron's 5 Day Oly Split
programs.author: Aaron
programs.description: Aaron's 5-day Olympic weightlifting split. Three technical platform days - snatch development, competition lifts, and a clean & jerk + squat-strength day - built around ramping singles and doubles up to a top set, plus two accessory days hammering hamstrings, posterior chain and core. The weights shown are Aaron's working numbers; read each exercise's note for the full set-by-set ramp and scale it to your own maxes.

programs.name: Top-Set Powerbuilding 5-Day
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A 5-day powerbuilding split: each main lift (squat, bench, behind-the-neck press, deadlift) is worked up to one heavy top set of 2-8 reps, then backed off with hypertrophy volume in the 8-15 range. Legs on day 1, a competition-style bench/triceps day, a shoulder day, a big deadlift-and-back day, and a lighter chest-and-arms pump day to finish the week.

programs.name: 5x Upper Lower

programs.description: A 5-day upper/lower split. Three lower/upper alternations plus a dedicated delts, rear-delt & grip day. Every session opens with a prehab warm-up, moves into primary lifts while you're freshest, then finishes with antagonist supersets (paired movements marked in each exercise's notes). Everything is prescribed at 2 sets of 6-12 reps - pick a load you can control across that range and add a little each week.

programs.name: Carpark Bodybuilding
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: A six-day, old-time-strongman body-part split run Sunday through Friday. Zercher stones, Kelly snatches, rings and bands sit alongside the barbell, and the small stuff most programs skip - neck, forearms, tibialis, ankles - gets its own dedicated block. Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday each carry two sessions (marked in the notes), so train them back to back or split them across the day. Exercises sharing a letter in the source are supersets; each one's note names its pair. Descending ladders like 20/15/12/8 mean one set per number - add load as the reps come down. Runs 8 weeks; add a little weight or a rep each week.

programs.name: Silver-Era Space Marine
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: Four rotating days - Confirmed Sasquatch, Bro Day, Quads/Abs/Calves and IRL Space Marine - run 2-4 days on, 1-2 days off. Aim to get all four sessions in within a 10-day window at most. Carpark strongman meets classic bodybuilding: Zercher deadlifts, Kelly snatches and overhead walks alongside incline presses, preacher curls and calf work. Can be combined with other programs for core, mobility and cardio - avoid stacking it with another intensive lifting program. Descending ladders like 12-15/8-12/5-8 mean one set per number; RPE targets above 10 mean taking the set past clean failure. Runs 8 weeks.

programs.name: Bronze Era Basics
programs.author: Wild Odds
programs.description: Three full-body days built on the basics: press, row, squat, bench, deadlift and pull-up, with Zercher squats, pullovers and loaded-stretch work rounding them out. Every lift has a barbell-free substitution in its notes, so the whole thing runs in a home gym with dumbbells. Load is prescribed by reps in reserve - the RPE target shown is the same thing inverted (RPE 9 = 1 RIR), and each note restates the original RIR. Later exercises marked as supersets or trisets run back to back with minimal rest, then loop. Runs 8 weeks; add load whenever you beat the top of a rep range at target RIR.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. Allow the torso to rise as needed, but try to avoid using leg drive and excessive momentum to cheat. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbells.

exercises.name: Arched Floor Press
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. You may take these out of a rack or begin with a hip thrust, but make sure the plates you use allow clearance for your body, or else get a spotter. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbell bench press.

exercises.name: Pullovers
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. Start light and focus on technique. Sink your hips as low as comfortable and allow the weight to pull your arms down as low as possible without bending them. You should feel a stretch in the area of your ribcage.

exercises.name: Zercher Squat
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. Try to use a more upright torso style for these. If you don't have a barbell, do goblet squats.

exercises.name: Barbell Strict Press
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbells. I recommend beginning these from the floor with a power clean if possible (1 clean per set), but if not, a rack is fine.

exercises.name: Pull Ups
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. Use band or machine assistance if unable to complete at least 5 reps on the first set unassisted. If this is not possible, use lat pulldowns.

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. 2 mins rest. If unable to complete at least 5 reps unassisted, use band or machine assistance. If you can get more than 20 reps, add weight next time if possible.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: 2 RIR. 2 mins rest. Barbell or dumbbells are both fine. Pay attention to technique, emphasising stretch on the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Barbell Squats
exercises.notes: 2 RIR. 2 mins rest. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbell goblet squats. I recommend a high bar style, but low bar is fine if that is more comfortable. Feel free to use heel elevation if needed.

exercises.name: Side Bend
exercises.notes: 2 RIR. Triset F1. Go straight to F2 (Russian Twist) with minimal rest.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.notes: 2 RIR. Triset F2. Per side. Go straight to F3 (Jefferson Curl) with minimal rest.

exercises.name: Jefferson Curl
exercises.notes: 5 RIR. 2 mins rest. Triset F3. Then restart from F1 (Side Bend). Use dumbbells if you don't have a barbell.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. Start light and focus on technique. Sink your hips as low as comfortable and allow the weight to pull your arms down as low as possible without bending them. You should feel a stretch in the area of your ribcage.

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. Superset C1. Go straight to C2 (Dumbbell Incline Curl) with minimal rest between sets. I recommend beginning these from the floor with a power clean if possible (1 clean per set), but if not, a rack is fine. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbells.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
exercises.notes: 0 RIR. 2 mins rest. Superset C2. Then return to C1 (Push Press). Sink into the deepest stretch possible at the bottom of every rep. Go to failure on the last two sets.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.notes: 2 RIR. 2 mins rest. Work up to 3 sets of 4-8. If you don't have a barbell, use dumbbells — and if they aren't heavy enough to challenge you in conventional deadlifts, do Romanian deadlifts.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: 1 RIR. Triset E1. Go straight to E2 (Windmill) with minimal rest. If no dumbbells heavy enough are available, you can use a barbell held in the top position of a curl.

exercises.name: Windmill
exercises.notes: 5 RIR. Triset E2. Go straight to E3 (Hanging Knee Raise) with minimal rest. Use a dumbbell instead of a barbell. Start very light and only go down as far as is comfortable. It is OK to bend the off-side knee.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.notes: 0 RIR. 2 mins rest. Triset E3. Then return to E1 (Goblet Squat).

programs.name: JPShuru x V1NLAND
programs.author: JPShuru x V1NLAND
programs.description: A 6-day body-part split built around five main lifts - incline bench, pull-ups, back squat, seated overhead press and deadlift - each run on the 12-week linear progression: add sets (weeks 1-3), add reps (weeks 4-6), add weight while dropping sets (weeks 7-9), then rebuild the sets at the new weight (weeks 10-12). Each main lift's coach notes give that week's sets, reps and weight jump; you choose your own starting weight. After week 12 the progression loops back to phase 1 at the heavier weight. Accessories, jumps, sprints and a Norwegian 4x4 conditioning finisher round out each day. Where a target says 'about', treat the rep number as a guide, not a hard stop.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few lighter ramp-up sets first - they don't count.

exercises.name: Push Up
exercises.notes: Sets and reps not given in the source - as many good reps as you can.

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.notes: One set per number: 20, then 15, then 15.

exercises.name: Machine Row
exercises.notes: Max out: as many reps as you can on each of the 3 sets.

exercises.name: Pull Up
exercises.notes: Bodyweight to start. Once the reps are easy, the target weight is load added with a dip belt.

exercises.name: Zercher Shrug
exercises.notes: About 20 reps. Bar held in the crook of the elbows.

exercises.name: Norwegian 4x4 Intervals
exercises.notes: 4 minutes hard (about 85-95% of max heart rate), then 3 minutes easy. Bike, rower or incline treadmill.

exercises.name: Golf Swing Warm-Up
exercises.notes: Warm-up only - sets and reps not given in the source. Easy swings to open the hips.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.notes: EMOM: start a set every minute, on the minute.

exercises.name: Hill Sprint
exercises.notes: Each rep: build up speed for 20 m, then go all-out for 20 m. Walk back down to recover.

programs.name: JPShuru x V1NLAND + 3x2 days per week
programs.author: JPShuru x V1NLAND
programs.description: The JPShuru x V1NLAND program reorganised into three sessions run twice a week: Chest, Arms & Abs / Back & Shoulders / Legs. The leg days are unchanged. Chest and arms are split so each session pairs a press with the triceps and biceps work that complements it, and back and shoulders are split so the pull-up variations and the two main presses are spread across the week rather than stacked. Every session has one main lift at most - incline bench, pull-ups, back squat, seated overhead press and deadlift - each on the 12-week linear progression: add sets (weeks 1-3), add reps (weeks 4-6), add weight while dropping sets (weeks 7-9), then rebuild the sets at the new weight (weeks 10-12). Each main lift's coach notes give that week's sets, reps and weight jump; you choose your own starting weight. After week 12 it loops back to phase 1 at the heavier weight.
